questions.q: Ethanoic acid undergoes Hell-Volhard Zelinsky reaction but methanoic acid does not, because of
options: presence of $\alpha-\mathrm{H}$ atom in ethanoic acid
absence of $\alpha-\mathrm{H}$ atom in ethanoic acid
higher acidic strength of ethanoic acid than methanoic acid
presence of $\alpha-\mathrm{H}$ atom in methanoic acid
questions.solution: Ethanoic acid has $\alpha-\mathrm{H}$ atom, thus it undergoes Hell-Volhard Zelinsky reaction. Whereas methanoic acid does not has $\alpha-\mathrm{H}$ atom, thus it does not give this test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
\( 25 $\mathrm{ cm}^{3}$\) of oxalic acid completely neutralized \( 0.064 $\mathrm{ g}$\) of sodium hydroxide. Molarity of the
oxalic acid solution is
questions.solution:
Given,
$V$ (oxalic acid) $=25 \mathrm{ cm}^{3}W(N a O H)=0.064 gM$ (oxalic acid) $=?$
Since, moles of oxalic acid $=$ mole of $N a O HV$ (oxalic acid) $\times N$ (oxalic acid) $=\frac{w}{M}(N a O H)\Rightarrow N$ ( oxalic acid) $=\frac{0.064 \times 1000}{25 \times 40}=0.064$
Normality $=$ Molarity $\times$ Basicity
\Rightarrow Molarity $=\frac{0.064}{2}=0.32$
Note: Basicity of oxalic acid is 2

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The ratio of heats liberated at \( 298 $\mathrm{~K}$\) from the combustion of one \( $\mathrm{kg}$\) of coke and by burning
water gas obtained from \( 1 $\mathrm{~kg}$\) of coke is
(Assume coke to be \( 100 \% \) carbon.)
(Given enthalpies of combustion of \( $\mathrm{CO}_{2}, \mathrm{CO}$\) and \( $\mathrm{H}_{2}$\) as \( 393.5 $\mathrm{~kJ},$285 $\mathrm{~kJ},$285 $\mathrm{~kJ}$\) respectively
all at \( 298 \) K.)
questions.solution:
One kg of coke $=\frac{1000}{12}=83.33$ moles of carbon By burning of one kg of coke
$\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{O}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_{2} ; \Delta_{c} \mathrm{H}=83.33 \times 393.5 \mathrm{ kJ} \rightarrow(1)$
Coke
By burning of water gas so obtain
$\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{CO}+\mathrm{H}_{2}+\mathrm{O}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} ; \Delta_{c} \mathrm{H}=83.33 \times 283.5 \mathrm{ kJ}+83.33 \times 285.5 \mathrm{ kJ} \rightarrow(2)=83.33 \times 569 \mathrm{ kJ}$
Divide Eq. (1) by Eq. (2), we get
$=\frac{83.33 \times 393.5 \mathrm{ kJ}}{83.33 \times 569 \mathrm{ kJ}}=0.69: 1$
Therefore, the ratio of heat liberated is $0.69: 1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Chloroacetic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid. This can be explained using
questions.solution: -Cl is an electron withdrawing (ie, $-I$ showing) group. It withdraws electrons when attached to the carboxylic acid and decreases the electron density on the oxygen atom. This will facilitate the release of $\mathrmH^{+}$ by making $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond more polar and thus $-\mathrm{Cl}$ increases the acidity of acetic acid when attached at, $\alpha$ position because of -I effect.
